lorenz.title: A little chaos
lorenz.caption: A rotating view of the Lorenz attractor.
lorenz.description: A deterministic Lorenz system is integrated with small Euler steps, then projected into two dimensions. EasyCanvas supplies the coordinates and drawing loop; the attractor and projection are ordinary JavaScript. The changing colors show progress along the trajectory. This is a visual experiment, not a numerical solver for scientific use.

interference.title: Waves colliding
interference.caption: Move the pointer to move one wave source.
interference.description: Two radial sine waves overlap. At each grid cell, their amplitudes add and map to a color. Move your pointer across the plot to move one source. This uses the exposed canvas context for the colored cells and EasyCanvas inverse scales to convert their positions into data coordinates. Reduced-motion preferences freeze time while keeping pointer interaction.

sunflower.title: The golden-angle garden
sunflower.caption: Hundreds of dots. One surprisingly good angle.
sunflower.description: Each seed is placed at a radius proportional to the square root of its index, with successive angles separated by the golden angle. The resulting spiral pattern resembles phyllotaxis in plants. EasyCanvas scales place the seeds; native canvas arcs keep the dots round in pixel space. Move across the plot to nudge the angle and see the pattern reorganize.

spirograph.title: A pocket spirograph
spirograph.caption: Layered parametric loops, slowly breathing.
spirograph.description: A rolling-circle formula produces a hypotrochoid. Several colored versions of the curve are drawn with a small phase offset that changes over time. All coordinates are passed through EasyCanvas drawLine; there is no chart-specific helper or extra dependency. Reduced-motion preferences hold the phase still.

fractal-tree.title: A tree that leans toward you
fractal-tree.caption: Recursion, one branch at a time.
fractal-tree.description: Each branch draws itself once, then calls itself for two shorter branches. That recursion is what makes fractal trees. Every segment goes through drawLine in data coordinates, with its line width set by depth so the trunk stays thick and the twig tips stay thin. Move across the plot and the canopy leans toward your pointer. A slow gust keeps the branches moving, and reduced-motion preferences hold the wind still.

histogram.title: Histogram
histogram.caption: How often did each value occur?
histogram.description: Pass raw numbers. Bins default to the square root of the sample size. Set bins, range, or density when you need more control.

pie.title: Pie chart
pie.caption: A quick look at the parts of a whole.
pie.description: Pass nonnegative values. Each slice has a legend entry and a hover tooltip with its name, value, and percentage. Set showLabels, showLegend, or showTooltips to false to hide each feature. Customize text with labelFormatter and tooltipFormatter.

donut.title: Donut chart
donut.caption: Same proportions, room in the middle.
donut.description: Donut charts share the pie settings, legends, and hover tooltips. The example hides labels inside the ring. Toggle showLabels or customize the hole using innerRadius.

box.title: Box and whisker
box.caption: Compare distributions and spot outliers.
box.description: Pass one array or a map of named groups. Boxes show the middle 50%, with a median line and whiskers to the last observations within 1.5 interquartile ranges. Points beyond that are shown separately.

scatter.title: Scatter plot
scatter.caption: Plot paired values without connecting them.
scatter.description: Give scatterPlot xs and ys arrays. Set radius in CSS pixels, or supply radii for a bubble plot.

bubble.title: Bubble plot
bubble.caption: Give each observation a third dimension.
bubble.description: Supply one radius per x/y pair. Radii use CSS pixels. Use square-root radii when you want circle area to represent magnitude.

area.title: Area chart
area.caption: Three series, stacked or independently filled.
area.description: Compare three sources of power. Set stacked to false for overlapping independent areas, or keep just one output for a single area. Each series gets a theme color and legend entry. The commented options show how to hide axes, legends, or controls.

heatmap.title: Heatmap
heatmap.caption: A grid of values becomes a field of color.
heatmap.description: Pass a two-dimensional array in row order. Missing or non-finite cells are skipped. Set colors for a palette or colorScale(value, fraction) for continuous color.

music.title: Music visualizer
music.caption: A live spectrum and waveform, driven by your music.
music.description: Press Play for a little homemade loop, or open an audio file from your device. Web Audio supplies the frequency spectrum and waveform; EasyCanvas draws them. The animated preview is silent until you start playback. Files stay in your browser. Try changing fftSize, smoothingTimeConstant, or the band colors in the code.
